name: Hydrate, wax and asphaltene management (inhibitors, heating, pigging)
aliases: Hydrate, wax and asphaltene management (inhibitors, heating, pigging)
principle: Hydrates form at high pressure and low temperature from light gases and can plug lines; one volume of hydrate holds 160 to 180 volumes of methane. They are managed with methanol or MEG injection, low-dosage and anti-agglomerant chemicals, insulation, heating and depressurisation, while wax is managed by pigging, insulation and heating.

process_steps.name: Inject inhibitors at the wellhead or manifold
Pig and heat lines as needed

performance.metric: methane held by one volume of hydrate

source.note: Journal of Petroleum Technology, Flow assurance: hydrates and paraffin management

performance.basis: case study flowlines; blockage 15,000 ft from wellhead

limitations: Anti-agglomerant failure can plug lines quickly
